text:
alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's runtime rollout we see an 8-12% tail latency regression on multi-GPU inference (4xA100). Repro in perf harness. Nvprof/Nsight traces show longer gaps where GPUs are idle waiting on a slab sync/allreduce. Putting captures here for triage.

alex: Capture commands I ran:
```
nvprof --profile-child-processes --print-gpu-trace -o nvprof_out.nvvp ./tools/perf_harness --config cfg/4gpu.json
nsight-systems --capture-range=nvtx --output nsight_nsight.qdrep ./tools/perf_harness --config cfg/4gpu.json
``` 

alex: Short custom-timer dump (median over 200 steps):
```
step_ms: 12.3
compute_ms: 10.2
kv_slab_drain_ms: 3.9   # baseline was ~1.2ms
allreduce_wait_ms: 2.8  # baseline ~0.9ms
other_ms: 0.3
``` 

maria: yikes. which commit rolled? I think kernel-selector switch landed in runtime @ 1803400xxx. Did that change quant/kern selection or fallback paths?

alex: yes merged yesterday afternoon — sha: d4f3b8e. It changed heuristics to prefer small-block GEMMs for attention on short sequences. Suspect it increased number of kernel launches which may be preventing overlap.

tony: nvprof timeline shows many tiny kernels for attention forward/backward. Also NVLINK activity has more frequent allreduce bursts. Might be more frequent cross-slab barrier calls.

sam: that matches my local repro — when we pick small-block GEMMs we get more fragmentation of KV writes, so slab drains happen more often instead of coalescing. batching heuristic could be triggering more flushes for mixed-length batches.

jessie: can you paste a short slice of the nsight timeline? which layers show the stalls (TP/PP boundary or after attention)?

alex: pasted snippet from nsight (condensed):
```
GPU0: compute(ATTN_k0) -> kernel chain -> kv_write -> nvtx:slab_drain -> allreduce -> compute(ATTN_k1)
GPU1: compute(...) -> idle 2.6ms -> allreduce
Observation: slab_drain occurs mid-layer for many micro-batches; overlap is poor because kernels are tiny.
```

tony: try forcing old kernel selector to confirm: set RUNTIME_KERNEL_HINT=legacy_smallbmm and re-run. If tail goes away, root cause is kernel selection fragmentation.

maria: also check NCCL algorithm selection. If we switch to ring vs tree it changes collective startup latency. run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and NCCL_ALGO=tree to compare.

sam: quick experiment results (local, 4xA100, 32 batch):
```
baseline (pre-change): tail 4.1% CPU/quantiles, kv_slab_drain_ms 1.2
with new selector: tail 12.4%, kv_slab_drain_ms 3.9
forcing legacy selector: tail 4.3%, kv_slab_drain_ms 1.3
NCCL_ALGO=tree reduced allreduce_wait_ms by ~0.6ms
``` 

perf-bot: synthetic sweep summary uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/1803456789/scan.csv — shows correlation between micro-kernel count and allreduce tail.

jessie: hypothesis: kernel selector change -> more micro kernels per attention -> more frequent KV slab writes -> slab drain triggers collective more often -> less compute/comm overlap -> tail regressions. Also batching heuristic exacerbates it by not merging short seqs into same micro-batch.

alex: agreed. proposed action items:
- revert selector to legacy in canary for a day (sam)
- add a defensive coalescing step: delay slab drain by up to 0.5ms to aggregate micro-batches when safe (engineering POC) (tony)
- add a custom timer around slab drain and collective start/finish and emit to console when >1ms (jessie)
- run full nsight capture and provide the qdrep link for deeper waterfall (maria)

sam: started a quick revert branch and running 100 iters now. will post results in ~10m

deploy-bot: deploy d4f3b8e -> prod finished 2026-03-17T21:14:08Z :rocket:

alex: thanks. if revert confirms, we need a follow-up RFC to change selector — we can rework batching + coalescing first.

sam: update: revert run shows kv_slab_drain_ms back to ~1.25 and tail down to ~4.5%. nvprof dumps in s3://redwood-perf/1803456789/revert_nvp.nvvp

maria: great repro. after we add timers and coalescing POC, let's also evaluate NCCL_ALGO variations and consider a fallback policy in runtime (if slab drain rate > X, force legacy kernels).

jessie: I'll add the timers this morning and wire alerts if slab_drain_ms spikes in canary. Also adding an opt-in flag to batch coalescer.

alex: perfect — assign follow-ups in the perf issue. thanks team :thumbsup!
